writeup.key_factor: New Orleans QB Tyler Shough is playing with two broken bones in his non-throwing hand (Schefter/ESPN), the Saints have lost three straight and sit 1-4, and the Giants are 4-1 ATS with a 3-0 ATS home mark. The raw model makes New York 66.1%; we discount it to 59.4% (fair -146) for the QB situation on both sides before calling it the day's Platinum — still the highest win probability on the board, selected under Growth Mode.
writeup.risk: The market has this near a pick'em for a reason: New York's wins have come by the skin of their teeth, QB Dart is on IR (Winston starts) and Brian Burns is on IR. The edge holds at -129 or better; below that price the play loses its value.

writeup.key_factor: Lamar Jackson is OUT (ankle, second straight game) and Huntley starts for Baltimore, who are also missing pieces up front. Cleveland is a textbook divisional home dog: 6-0 ATS at home vs the AFC North and 2-0 straight up as a home underdog this year. The model makes the Browns 47.4% (fair +111) against a +151 market — the cleanest classic edge on today's board, no adjustments needed.
writeup.risk: RB1 Judkins is questionable and Cleveland's interior defensive line is depleted (Hall Jr. and Davis out, Graham questionable) against Derrick Henry. If Judkins is ruled out, this play gets re-evaluated before kickoff.

writeup.key_factor: This price is already adjusted for Baker Mayfield being OUT: the model drops Tampa Bay to 49.1% (fair +104) with rookie Jalon Daniels making his third start. Daniels already won on the road at Dallas (19/25, no turnovers) behind Bowles' ground game, Tampa is at home, and Pittsburgh's secondary is banged up (Ramsey and Dean questionable, Elliott out). At +121 the adjusted number still clears with edge.
writeup.risk: The whole discount is the quarterback: if Daniels turns it over early, the adjusted model breaks. S Winfield Jr. is out for Tampa, and Tampa wind is on alert (sustained teens, gusts upper-20s) — a pre-game weather recheck is mandatory.
